title: The series
body:
I trained as a doctor and now work in US healthcare operations: coding, billing audit, risk adjustment, care coordination. Every day I see problems that a small, well-built tool could fix.

So over the past few weeks I've been building them, using AI coding tools (Claude Code) to go from idea to a live demo in days instead of months.

Eight projects so far, all on public or synthetic data:
• DecodeMyBill: explains a medical bill and flags duplicate charges
• Denial Co-pilot: turns a claim denial code into a fix or an appeal
• CivicFeed: what 721 public comments said about a CMS rule
• Discharge Gap Checker: what a nursing home needs but didn't get
• Medicaid Renewal Buddy: New York's 2027 work requirements, in plain language
• Sprain or Fracture?: the Ottawa Rules as a self-check
• Integrative Case Sheet and SIH 2026 Explorer

In the following days I'll share them one at a time: the problem, what I built, and what I learned.

All of them are here: https://rutulpatel.dev

#HealthInformatics #HealthTech #DigitalHealth #BuildInPublic

title: DecodeMyBill
body:
A sample ER bill: $3,974. What Medicare would pay for the same services: $359.

It also has three errors in it: a metabolic panel billed twice (the basic panel is already part of the comprehensive one), a blood draw billed three times, and a duplicate chest X-ray. That's about $668 the patient shouldn't owe.

These are hard to spot because bills are written in CPT codes. Few patients ever dispute a bill, even though many who do get it corrected.

DecodeMyBill takes a pasted bill or a photo of one and:
• explains each line in plain English
• compares each charge with Medicare's 2026 rate, calculated from the official CMS fee schedules
• flags duplicates and double billing
• drafts a dispute letter and a phone script

Two design choices: all the price math is done in code rather than by an AI model, and the bill never leaves your browser.

Try it with a sample bill: https://decodemybill.vercel.app
Code: https://github.com/patelr31/decodemybill

#MedicalBilling #HealthcareCosts #PatientAdvocacy #HealthTech

title: Denial Co-pilot
body:
"CO-50 N115." To most people that's noise. To a billing team it means the payer considers the service not medically necessary under a Medicare Local Coverage Determination, and the provider is liable.

Every denial on a remittance arrives as codes like these. Deciding what to do next (fix and resubmit, appeal, bill another payer, or write it off) usually depends on someone who has worked hundreds of them.

Denial Co-pilot puts that on one screen. Enter the codes and it shows:
• a plain-English explanation
• who is liable, based on the group code
• the recommended next step and a checklist
• the 120-day Medicare appeal deadline, counted from the denial date
• a draft appeal letter or corrected-claim checklist

Testing it on ten made-up denials caught two mistakes in my first version. A CO-group non-covered denial can never be billed to the patient, and a signed ABN turns CO-50 into PR-50. Both rules are now built in.

https://denial-copilot.vercel.app

#RevenueCycle #MedicalBilling #ClaimDenials #HealthTech

title: CivicFeed
body:
721 people and organizations commented on CMS's proposed rule on interoperability and prior authorization for drugs. I wanted to see what they actually said.

What the comments showed:
• 36% came from coordinated campaigns, mainly two: a form letter sent 236 times, and a template filed by 16 health centers and their associations, each with its own name swapped in. Exact-match deduplication misses that second one; it takes fuzzy matching on shared wording.
• Almost nobody opposed the rule. The clearest "withdraw the proposal" comment was about a different rule and was probably misfiled.
• The real debate was timing. About 10 times more comments asked CMS to delay or phase in the October 2027 deadline than asked it to keep the date.

How it works: code handles what rules can (campaign detection, who is commenting, grouping into themes). AI labels and summarizes the themes but writes no numbers. Code then checks that every quote appears word for word in the original comment, and the build fails if one doesn't.

That last check is the part I'd reuse on any AI project.

https://civicfeed-six.vercel.app

#HealthPolicy #CMS #Interoperability #PriorAuthorization #AI

title: Discharge Gap Checker
body:
A patient arrives at a nursing home on a Friday evening. The discharge summary lists oxycodone, but there's no signed controlled-substance prescription. The facility pharmacy can't dispense it, and the patient misses their pain doses that night.

Gaps like this are common. In a national survey of nursing home Directors of Nursing (JAMA Network Open, 2021), behavioral status was missing for 68% of hospital–nursing home pairs, social status for 66%, and an after-hours hospital contact for 54%. Facilities spent about 6.5 hours a week chasing missing information.

The Discharge Gap Checker reads a pasted discharge summary and shows:
• which of those commonly missing items are absent
• safety flags: an opioid with no prescription, an antibiotic with no stop date, a pending result with no one named to follow up
• a list of callback questions, safety items first

I tested it on five synthetic summaries with gaps planted on purpose, and it caught all of them.

If you work in post-acute admissions, I'd like to hear what else you'd check.

https://discharge-gap.vercel.app

#CareTransitions #SkilledNursing #PostAcuteCare #PatientSafety

title: Medicaid Renewal Buddy
body:
From January 2027, many New York Medicaid members aged 19–64 face two changes: a work requirement (80 hours a month, or $580 in income) and renewals every 6 months instead of once a year. The state estimates nearly 2 million New Yorkers are in the affected group.

From my time in care coordination, the usual pattern is a notice in confusing language, a missed deadline, and then a lapse in coverage.

This is a plain-language helper. A few questions show:
• whether the requirement applies to you, and whether an exception might (including the planned Bronx exception)
• how your income and hours add up, using the state's own conversion ($380 = 52 hours)
• what to have ready and when your renewal is due, with calendar reminders

It also covers one piece of good news: New York has a hold-harmless period, so nobody loses coverage over the work requirement before June 30, 2027.

Every eligibility rule links to its official source. It's educational, not legal advice.

https://medicaid-buddy.vercel.app

#Medicaid #NewYork #HealthEquity #HealthPolicy

title: Sprain or Fracture?
body:
You twist your ankle. Is it a sprain or a fracture? Usually the only way to know is an ER visit and an X-ray, and most turn out to be sprains.

Emergency clinicians already have a tool for this: the Ottawa Ankle Rules. A few questions (where it hurts, whether specific bony points are tender, whether you could take 4 steps) decide who needs an X-ray. In pooled studies they catch about 98% of fractures.

I turned them into a guided self-check for Razorpay's Fix My Itch problem: "Why is distinguishing sprains from fractures impossible without costly hospital visits?"

The order of the questions matters most:
1. Warning signs first (deformity, a numb or cold foot, a high-energy injury): go to the ER
2. Cases the rules don't cover (children, older injuries, head injuries): see a clinician
3. Only then the Ottawa questions, with a diagram of where to press

The tool says plainly that these rules were designed for a clinician's exam, so a self-check is less certain. If in doubt, get it checked.

https://patelr31.github.io/sprain-check/

#EmergencyMedicine #EvidenceBasedMedicine #DigitalHealth #FixMyItch

title: Integrative Case Sheet and SIH 2026 Explorer
body:
Two connected builds, because one led to the other.

First, a dashboard of all 226 Smart India Hackathon 2026 problem statements. Two findings: AI appears in 44% of the problems, and the theme labels aren't reliable. A clinical-trials dashboard was filed under Space Technology, and land-record digitization under MedTech.

Filtering by health instead of by theme turned up SIH26047, "Patient Case-Taking Software" from the Ministry of Ayush, so I built it:
• a guided case sheet for clinicians who practice Ayush and modern medicine together: history, vitals, a Prakriti screen and the eight-fold Ashtavidha examination
• diagnoses coded in ICD-10-CM from a verified list (the check caught one code that wasn't billable)
• red-flag checks that prompt a modern referral, such as chest pain on exertion
• export as a FHIR R4 bundle with LOINC-coded vitals, so the record can move between systems

https://integrative-case-sheet.vercel.app
https://sih-2026-explorer-tau.vercel.app

#FHIR #Interoperability #Ayush #DigitalHealth #SmartIndiaHackathon
